name: Thomas Scott (India) Ltd
title: Thomas Scott (India) Ltd - 533941 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Digital apparel retailer with no capacity-discipline signal; Q1 revenue +22% to INR 66 cr with EBITDA margin 13.07%, but growth was bought via marketing and wholesale aggregator sales, and a fire-insurance claim keeps debt elevated.

utilisation.quote: our manufacturing capacities are fully occupied. So, we largely have to produce in capital capacities, rent out or pay job work

capex.quote: The capital expenses are not that high in our model.

triggers.label: Price cuts withheld; marketing used instead
triggers.quote: we are focused on protecting our realizations rather than pursuing volume through aggressive discounting

triggers.label: Finance cost ~3x YoY on working capital
triggers.quote: the finance cost has increased to about Rs. 1 crore and it is almost a 3x increase from the same quarter previous year

triggers.label: Online growth slowed; Q1 ROI growth weak
triggers.quote: we have seen a very drastic drop in ROI growth in B2C licensed brand and our own brand

guidance.value: healthy, similar to current, consistent improvement

So, I do not want to give a specific number.
We want to be the number one multi-brand online retailer globally.

summary.headline: Thomas Scott Q1 FY27 revenue rose 22% YoY to INR 66 crore and EBITDA margin was 13.07%, as management chose to hold prices over discounting.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations was INR 66 crore (+22% YoY), EBITDA INR 9 crore (+43% YoY, margin 13.07%) and PAT about INR 5 crore (+54% YoY, margin 8.21%). Management said subdued price elasticity led it to protect realisations and shift spend from discounts to performance marketing, which it said lifted gross margins. Wholesale-style aggregator sales now make up about 40% of Thomas Scott brand revenue. Finance costs rose sharply on working capital tied to a fire-related insurance claim that is still pending.

segments.name: Thomas Scott (own brand)
segments.commentary: Revenue close to INR 25 crore, up 34% YoY, driven by online-first approach, rapid launches and data-led merchandising. About 40% of brand revenue came via aggregator bulk orders booked at wholesale prices under marketplace channel.

segments.name: Licensed and other brands
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 38 crore, up 14% YoY, supported by marketplace relationships and premiumisation. Dockers licence agreements expected to contribute meaningfully in coming quarters.

segments.name: Contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: Revenue INR 4 crore, up 33% YoY, on higher capacity utilisation and marquee customer relationships.

segments.name: Women's wear (newer category)
segments.commentary: Piloted for about two quarters; management says most revenue so far came from testing. Cited as a growth pillar at around 13% of Q1 revenue per analyst question, not disputed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 target: continue the growth pace of the last two years, with similar margins (confirmed on Q&A).

Management expects healthy margins and aims for consistent EBITDA margin improvement through the year, but may reinvest margin in growth; the 12-15% EBITDA margin range was cited by an analyst and not disputed.
Price discounting may return in Q2-Q4, particularly festive H2, where management expects better ROI.
Women's wear could reach 2x to 3x current revenue in about a year, with gradual scaling rather than sudden growth.
Insurance claim (fire incident, about INR 21 crore of stock insured) expected to settle soon; debt and interest cost expected to normalise after realisation.
capex_capacity: Manufacturing capacity is fully utilised for the last few quarters; the company uses job work and rented capacity to meet demand.
Manufacturing footprint across Sholapur, Bangalore and Gurgaon, with fulfilment centres across India.
Target manufacturing mix: about 50% in-house, 35-40% outsourced (per-piece labour charges, with in-house quality control), and about 5% bought-out goods.
Capex is consistent each quarter but described as modest; the main effort is workforce hiring, training and line efficiency.
Offline stores (Bangalore) are EBITDA positive but ROCE is below online opportunities, so capital is directed online; new stores will be selective.
demand_pricing: Price elasticity was subdued in Q1; management says demand exists but price cuts did not earn adequate ROI, so it chose performance marketing over discounts.
Management attributed cautious sentiment partly to global macro conditions, including LPG shortages; said August sentiment is positive.
Customer acquisition cost is about 4-6% of GMV, with the quarter at the higher end; no precise CAC or payback figure was given.
Wholesale-style aggregator sales booked at B2B price, about INR 10 crore in Q1, equivalent to about INR 15 crore NSV per management; management says these are EBITDA-margin neutral.
Management claims demand exceeds supply capability.
Q1 is an end-of-season sale quarter in which the company chose not to discount heavily.

qa_highlights.question: How do women's wear unit economics and repeat purchases compare with men's wear, and what share is targeted?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said unit economics are neutral to favourable versus men's wear, with better return-cost control. Core products such as bottomwear and basic tops show repeat behaviour similar to men's; no share target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Quick commerce strategy and economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Main partner is M-Now (Myntra) at neutral unit economics with no extra fee. Broader quick commerce strategy is still nascent; core categories to be evaluated over the next six to nine months.

qa_highlights.question: Bangalore store performance and expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Stores are EBITDA positive but ROCE is lower than online, so capital goes online. Offline may scale in FY28; new stores will be selective.

qa_highlights.question: Why did revenue growth slow in ROI for licensed and own brands?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is a margin-pressured end-of-season sale quarter; it chose not to match discounts and invested in marketing instead. Lost revenue could be recovered in festive H2.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company still on track for prior revenue run-rate and margins in FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Targets unchanged: same growth rate as the last few years and healthy margins, with margin improvement sought while reserving margin for growth investment.

qa_highlights.question: Fire insurance claim and finance cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Insurance claim (about INR 21 crore of stock, fully insured) is in process; elevated working-capital loans raised to fund inventory are expected to fall once the claim is realised. Exception provisions are small (INR 3-4 lakh).

qa_highlights.question: Dockers deal: B2B or B2C, and effect on premiumisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Dockers agreement is B2C-focused; B2B is used for long-run sourcing orders. More than 94% of revenue is B2C. Dockers fits the premiumisation strategy.

risks_watch: Finance cost rising sharply on working capital; normalisation depends on timing of the insurance claim settlement, which is still in process.
Revenue growth is dependent on the timing of price reinvestment in H2 festive; if festive demand is weak, the growth catch-up may not happen.
Rising other expenses (marketing) and a higher CAC in Q1; watch whether gross margin gains hold as marketing spend rises.
Aggregator/wholesale channel share (about 40% of brand revenue) and its effect on reported revenue vs. NSV; the company reports B2B value, which understates headline sales.
Women's wear is still in a test-and-scale phase; scaling could strain returns and inventory.
Capacity is fully utilised, so growth depends on job-work and rented capacity.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the platform and long-term ambition, but defensive on Q1 growth, which management framed as a deliberate trade-off to protect price and margin. Evasive on specific CAC, payback, and insurance claim timing, citing process constraints.

financial_highlights.change: almost 3x YoY (per analyst; not contested by management)

financial_highlights.metric: Wholesale/aggregator revenue booked in Thomas Scott brand
financial_highlights.value: about INR 10 crore (approx. 40% of Thomas Scott revenue)
